project.title: Think it. Make it.
project.format: 2024 global brand-awareness campaign spanning OOH, transit placements, social crops, and an animated anthem

why: A strong campaign-visual reference because it shows how a famously minimal software brand can temporarily widen its visual language for public media without losing recognition. The system keeps Notion's illustration DNA, then adds close-profile crops, primary-color blocks, bespoke headlines, and one simple call-to-action so the campaign reads clearly from billboards down to phone-sized social posts.

artDirection.title: One imperative line anchors the whole rollout
artDirection.study: BUCK and Notion turned the campaign into a repeatable headline system around 'Think it. Make it.', then extended it into bespoke OOH copy about AI features without making the campaign read like a product-sheet explainer.
artDirection.reuse: When a product has many use cases, reduce the campaign to one short command and let supporting headlines flex around that core sentence.

artDirection.title: Move from full scenes to close profile portraits
artDirection.study: Notion's own write-up explains that the team moved away from distant full-body scenes and closer into side-profile illustrations so viewers could 'see their brains at work' and connect more quickly on billboards and transit media.
artDirection.reuse: Tighten illustration crops when a campaign has to read fast in public space and needs the character, not the environment, to carry the message.

artDirection.title: Abstract thinking visualized through the inside of the head
artDirection.study: The campaign uses cubist, Goldberg-like, and hand-drawn interior head imagery to represent thought, knowledge work, and AI assistance without resorting to literal interface mockups.
artDirection.reuse: Use one strong metaphorical picture system when the product story is abstract and would become flat if reduced to screens and feature labels.

artDirection.title: Selective primary colors break a monochrome brand out into the city
artDirection.study: Notion explains that its usual black-and-white language disappeared in busy urban contexts, so the campaign introduces bright yellow, blue, and red blocks while keeping the core drawing style intact.
artDirection.reuse: Let an otherwise restrained brand adopt a temporary signal palette for OOH if the rest of the brand assets are already highly recognizable.

channelFormats.title: Headline-first billboards and posters
channelFormats.notes: The campaign is designed for outdoor placements where the short tagline, tight illustration crop, and primary-color field do the first-read work before any secondary copy appears.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Keep the face, the thought-space, and one bold line intact so the layout survives very short viewing windows and long-distance reading.
channelFormats.reuse: Design the billboard/poster variant as the campaign's clarity test before expanding into richer digital formats.

channelFormats.title: Transit and street furniture adaptation
channelFormats.notes: Notion's July 10, 2024 post explicitly places the work on billboards in San Francisco, Tube stations in London, and bus stops in Seoul, proving the system can survive multiple public-media aspect ratios.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Treat profile direction, color blocks, and headline lockups as the invariant pieces while the surrounding negative space flexes per transit format.
channelFormats.reuse: Build one invariant reading spine for campaign media that has to move across bus shelters, platform posters, and other constrained public frames.

channelFormats.title: Social crops keep the same concept rather than shrinking the app UI
channelFormats.notes: BUCK describes the work as a suite of OOH illustrations and campaign outputs that scale into smaller digital placements without switching to literal software screenshots.
channelFormats.cropSystem: Use the same illustration logic and headline posture on smaller canvases so mobile audiences recognize the campaign as the same system, not a second art direction.
channelFormats.reuse: Resist replacing the core visual grammar with UI screenshots when adapting a broad campaign for social formats.

assets.notes: A short master tagline plus tailored sub-headlines turns a flexible product story into public-facing copy that reads quickly.
assets.reuse: Create one master imperative and derive concise variations instead of writing unrelated campaign headlines per channel.

assets.notes: Roman Muradov's illustrations remain the campaign's recognizability engine, but the tighter head-and-shoulders crops make them carry more emotional and narrative weight.
assets.reuse: Keep the signature illustration author while changing framing before replacing the visual language entirely.

assets.notes: The system adds saturated yellow, blue, and red blocks to a previously monochrome brand so the work can compete in cities and transit systems.
assets.reuse: Use a limited temporary palette as a campaign-only amplifier when the master brand is too quiet for OOH.

assets.notes: Simple geometric color fields and framing blocks give the hand-drawn imagery enough structure to scale cleanly across placements.
assets.reuse: Pair expressive illustration with blunt framing geometry so the campaign still reads as a system under heavy resizing and recropping.

motion.title: Animated anthem translates the static grammar into motion
motion.notes: BUCK describes an animated anthem that pulls the close crops, color palette, and conceptual storytelling into one succinct moving brand story for the launch.
motion.fallback: If a launch cannot fund a hero film, keep the same profile crops, color blocks, and imperative headline structure in static OOH and social frames.

implementation.format: Global brand-awareness campaign system for a software brand across outdoor, transit, social, and motion media
implementation.notes: This is strong enough for accepted status because the first-party sources are complementary: BUCK's case study shows the rollout breadth and credits, while Notion's official post published on July 10, 2024 explains the conceptual and compositional decisions behind the public campaign.
